title: Andy Carroll: Former England striker pleads not guilty to breaching non-molestation order
content:
Former England striker Andy Carroll has pleaded not guilty to breaching a non-molestation order.

Carroll appeared via video link at Chelmsford Crown Court on Wednesday and a trial date has been set at the same venue for January 18, 2027.

The 37-year-old, who currently plays for Dagenham & Redbridge, was arrested on April 27 last year, in relation to an alleged offence in the previous month.

In February this year, Carroll appeared at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court and indicated a not guilty plea, saying he wanted to have his case heard at a crown court rather than a magistrates’.

Judge Mary Loram KC ruled on Wednesday that Carroll will remain on conditional bail.

A non-molestation order is a court injunction that usually stops someone from contacting another person and may also ban them from going near their home or workplace.

Breaching such an order is a criminal offence, with penalties ranging from a fine to up to five years in prison for the most serious cases.

Carroll joined Dagenham, who play in the National League South — English football’s sixth tier — last summer, and has scored seven goals in 13 appearances.

His spell at the east London club has been disrupted by injury.

In January, he posted on his Instagram account that he had undergone surgery on a ligament injury and fracture. He had missed the start of the 2025-26 season with a hamstring injury.

Last week, Dagenham announced that Carroll had become a shareholder in the club.

In January 2011, Carroll became Liverpool’s record signing when he joined from Newcastle United in a £35million (now $48m) transfer.

Capped nine times by England, Carroll has also had spells at West Ham United, Reading and West Bromwich Albion, along with French clubs Amiens and Bordeaux.
